title: Napoleon and the end
hook: Reorganisation, a rival imperial title and the Rhine Confederation preceded the abdication.
notes: GHDI introduction for 1803, Habsburger House of Austria for 1804, primary abdication declaration for 1806. Napoleon’s pressure is explained through the Rhine union cited in the declaration; markers are political locators, not military movements. The declaration date uses Gregorian calendar. Coordinates are approximate named-place locators, not imported surveyed points. Modern borders are hidden. Event cards contain claim-level citations. The later term Holy Roman Empire must not be projected unchanged onto Charlemagne’s Frankish realm.

scenes.title: Reorganisation from within
scenes.text: The Final Recess of 1803 secularised church territories and reduced the number of independent imperial cities. Regensburg anchors the empire’s institutional setting; no speculative before-and-after borders are drawn.

scenes.title: Two imperial titles
scenes.text: In 1804 Francis adopted an Austrian imperial title while still Holy Roman Emperor. Vienna’s court therefore links two different offices, rather than a simple renaming of the same state.

scenes.title: Napoleon’s new political order
scenes.text: The Rhine Confederation separated participating states from the imperial structure in 1806. The regional locator deliberately avoids drawing an uncited outline of its membership.

scenes.title: An office is relinquished
scenes.text: Francis’s declaration of 6 August 1806, issued at Vienna, laid down the imperial crown and released estates and servants from their obligations. The sequence ends with a primary document, not an invented map of a final front line.
